newsitem.title: GERMANY: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND PULLS OFF SECOND WIN AT GARMISCH.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND PULLS OFF SECOND WIN AT GARMISCH.

text.p: France's Luc Alphand triumphed on one of the toughest mountains in Alpine skiing for the second consecutive day when he clinched his fourth downhill victory of the World Cup season on Saturday.

Alphand, who bounced back from his disappointing world championships with victory in Friday's super-G in the German resort, sped down an icy course in one minute 54.27 seconds, according to provisional results.

Italy's Pietro Vitalini, who had to ski twice after he was forced to halt his first run because a man got in his way on the piste, took second place in 1:54.85 with compatriot Italy's Kristian Ghedina third one hundredth of a second further behind.
The result helped Alphand to stretch his lead in both the overall World Cup standings and in the downhill standings where he is bidding for a third consecutive title.

The double in Garmisch-Partenkirchen marked a remarkable return to form for the 31-year-old Frenchman who crashed out of the downhill at this month's world championships in Sestriere and finished only 12th in the super-G.
